title: Perioperative antiplatelet management in ischaemic heart disease with left ventricular apical thrombus: complex fistula-in-ano surgery in a patient with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes and scabies
authors: Subhasis Mishra; Prof. Raghavendra Hegde; Bhimanagouda Veerabhadrappa Goudar; Shivarudrappa Mallikarjun Goornavar
journal: Journal of Drug Delivery and Therapeutics
abstract: Objective: To describe the pharmacotherapeutic and perioperative management of a patient in whom urgent drainage of a perianal abscess conflicted with the need for continued antiplatelet protection of a diseased left ventricle containing apical thrombus, and in whom uncontrolled diabetes and scabies further complicated treatment. Design: Single-patient case report from the surgical and medical units of a tertiary care teaching hospital in northern Karnataka, India, prepared from the hospital case record after written informed consent. Intervention: Multidisciplinary care involving cautious peri-procedural handling of clopidogrel and aspirin, continuation of anti-ischaemic therapy, transfer from oral antidiabetic drugs to a basal-bolus insulin regimen, empirical metronidazole-based broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, topical treatment for scabies, and fistulectomy with drainage under spinal anaesthesia. Main outcome measures: Perioperative cardiac events, bleeding complications, glycaemic control, wound healing and discharge status. Results: A 39-year-old man with ischaemic heart disease, an ejection fraction of 45% and a layered left ventricular apical thrombus presented with a perianal abscess overlying a complex trans-sphincteric fistula-in-ano. Glycated haemoglobin was 13.1%. Drainage was initially deferred while clopidogrel was withheld, and during this interval he developed a fresh anterior ischaemic event. After multidisciplinary optimisation, fistulectomy with drainage was performed under spinal anaesthesia. Recovery was uneventful, with no cardiac event, no significant bleeding and satisfactory wound healing. Conclusion: When thrombotic and haemorrhagic risks conflict, individualised timing of antithrombotic therapy and coordinated multidisciplinary planning, rather than reflexive withdrawal of antiplatelet drugs, allow necessary surgery to proceed safely. Keywords: clopidogrel, perianal abscess, perioperative care, left ventricular thrombus, spinal anaesthesia, insulin therapy

title: Hypocalcemic Cardiomyopathy Due to Multifactorial Disturbances in Calcium Homeostasis
authors: Satoshi Kurisu; Hitoshi Fujiwara
abstract: We report a case of hypocalcemic cardiomyopathy in a patient with a history of thyroid surgery. An inappropriately normal parathyroid hormone response, vitamin D deficiency, and potentially reduced calcium absorption associated with long-term proton pump inhibitor use were considered contributing factors to impaired calcium homeostasis. The patient presented with symptoms of heart failure, bronchospasm, and persistent hypocalcemia, accompanied by marked QT prolongation and left ventricular dysfunction. Treatment with alfacalcidol resulted in normalization of serum calcium levels, improvement in heart failure symptoms, and resolution of bronchospasm. Follow-up echocardiography at five months demonstrated partial improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction, while serum B-type natriuretic peptide levels gradually decreased over the seven-month follow-up period. In conclusion, hypocalcemia should be considered a potentially reversible cause of cardiomyopathy in patients with unexplained cardiac dysfunction. Our case highlights the importance of evaluating calcium homeostasis, particularly when risk factors for calcium deficiency are present.

title: Morphological and Morphometric Variations of Left Ventricular Papillary Muscles in Human Heart Specimens
authors: AZHAR QUDEER; YUGANTI VAIDY; Swati Thamke; VISHNU PAL; Harsha Atul Keche; Venkata Surya Kumar
journal: International Journal of Current Pharmaceutical Research
abstract: Objective: To describe the number, morphometry, shape and ventricular attachment of left ventricular papillary muscles and to compare anterolateral and posteromedial morphology in a human heart specimen series. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional anatomical study was performed on 38 preserved human heart specimens. Anterolateral and posteromedial belly number, mean length, mean breadth, shape and left ventricular wall thickness were analysed. Paired comparisons used exact Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, accessory-belly prevalence used an exact McNemar test, and Spearman correlations used 50,000 permutations with Holm correction. Results: Anterolateral observations were available in 37 specimens and posteromedial observations in 36; 109 individual bellies were recorded. mean anterolateral and posteromedial lengths were 2.64±0.61 cm and 2.55±0.73 cm, and breadths were 1.08±0.31 cm and 1.02±0.32 cm, respectively. Paired differences in number, length and breadth were not significant. Accessory bellies occurred in 38.9% of paired anterolateral observations and 52.8% of posteromedial observations (P=0.302). Cylindrical and conical forms predominated. Anterolateral breadth correlated inversely with belly number (rho=-0.554; Holm-adjusted P=0.0028) and positively with length (rho=0.616; Holm-adjusted P=0.0008). Conclusion: Left ventricular papillary muscles showed frequent numerical and shape variation, although paired anterolateral and posteromedial dimensions were similar. Recognition of this variability is relevant to mitral repair and replacement, post-infarction rupture, subvalvular surgery for outflow obstruction and papillary-muscle arrhythmia ablation.

title: Feasibility of AI-Guided Handheld Echocardiography for Rheumatic Heart Disease Screening by Non-Cardiologists in Rural Nepal: A Mixed-Methods Diagnostic Accuracy Study
authors: Husameddin Alattar; Dhyana Magesh; Angela Pal; Rache Mureau-Haines; Taylor Young; Keshet Ronen; David Zhang; Jay D. Pal
abstract: Background: Rheumatic heart disease remains a major cause of preventable morbidity and mortality in rural Nepal, where access to cardiovascular specialists and echocardiography is limited. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy and feasibility of AI-guided echocardiography performed by nurse practitioners for community-based RHD screening. Methods: We conducted a triangulation mixed-methods study (QUAN > qual) combining a paired cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study with semi-structured interviews during community screening camps in Damak, Nepal, in November 2025. Nurse practitioners performed AI-guided handheld echocardiography using EchoNous Kosmos Plus devices, with cardiologist overread serving as the comparator. Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and kappa. Interviews were analyzed thematically. Results: Of 90 participants enrolled, 76 were included in the final analysis. Mean age was 50.8 years, 57.8% were male, and 42.2% had undergone prior cardiac evaluation. Detection of any valvular lesion demonstrated 95.8% sensitivity and 100% specificity, with near-perfect agreement with cardiologist interpretation (?=0.97). Lesion-specific performance included mitral regurgitation sensitivity 66.7% and specificity 97.3% (?=0.55), mitral stenosis sensitivity 100% and specificity 97.2% (?=0.81), aortic regurgitation sensitivity 90.9% and specificity 96.9% (?=0.84), and tricuspid regurgitation sensitivity and specificity of 100% (?=1.00). Mean scan duration was 5.8 minutes. Portability, AI-assisted acquisition, and remote review facilitated implementation, while training needs, workflow constraints, and technical issues were barriers. Conclusions: AI-guided handheld echocardiography performed by nurses demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy and feasibility for rural RHD screening. AI-assisted task-shifting may expand access to early RHD detection in underserved settings.

title: Detecting low left ventricular ejection fraction from ECG using an interpretable and scalable predictor-driven framework: a model development and validation study
authors: Ya Zhou; Tianxiang Hao; Ziyi Cai; Haojie Zhu; Hejun He; Jia Liu; Xiaohan Fan; Jing Yuan
abstract: Background Low left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) frequently remains undetected until progression to symptomatic heart failure, underscoring the need for effective approaches to earlier detection of low LVEF. Although artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) has shown promise, existing approaches rely solely on end-to-end black-box models with limited interpretability or on tabular models with limited applicability. Methods In this retrospective multicohort study, we developed and validated a predictor-driven framework that reuses diagnostic scores of conventional ECG findings derived from an ECG foundation model for the detection of low LVEF. The foundation model was developed using 413,167 ECGs from four independent publicly available ECG-only datasets collected across multiple countries, locations, and time periods. The official test set of the EchoNext benchmark, comprising ECG–echocardiography (ECHO) pairs collected at Columbia University Irving Medical Center between 2008 and 2022, was used as the internal test set (n = 5442). We constructed an external test set (n = 16,017) from MIMIC-IV-ECG and related data, comprising ECG–clinical note (Note) pairs collected at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center between 2008 and 2019. The primary outcome was low LVEF (LVEF ≤ 45%), assessed by ECHO or Note documentation within one year after the ECG. The model-derived diagnostic scores for each ECG finding were evaluated for low LVEF discrimination in the internal and external test sets, neither of which was used to develop the ECG foundation model. We further trained tree-based models using these diagnostic representations on the official EchoNext training set (72,475 paired ECG–ECHO records), followed by evaluation on the internal and external test sets. Explainability analyses were performed to identify key predictive features and characterize ECG-related patterns associated with low LVEF. Findings Diagnostic scores for conventional ECG findings showed discriminative performance for low LVEF across cohorts, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values up to 81.0% for individual predictors. The tree-based model achieved an AUROC of 88.4% (95% confidence interval (CI), 87.1–89.5) in the internal cohort, outperforming the official end-to-end baseline on the EchoNext benchmark, and maintained discrimination in the external cohort, with an AUROC of 86.9% (86.2–87.7). Normal ECG (NORM), incomplete left bundle branch block (ILBBB), and ischemic changes in lateral leads (ISCLA) ranked 1–3 by internal single-predictor AUROC and had the same ranking in the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)–based analysis. Interpretation Diagnostic scores of conventional ECG findings from ECG foundation models contain information relevant to the detection of ventricular dysfunction. These representations can be directly reused for low LVEF detection and further integrated into interpretable predictive models, providing a scalable and extensible computational framework for existing AI-ECG systems. Future research should validate the framework in population-based screening settings and larger international cohorts. Funding This work was partially supported by the CAMS Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences and the National Natural Science Foundation of China.

title: Hemodynamic effects of cycle ergometry versus dynamic unilateral arm exercise during right heart catheterization: a prospective observational study
authors: Eugen Berezucki; Maria Heinrich; Alexander Rueß; Tobias J. Lange; Markus Perl; Stefan Stadler
abstract: BACKGROUND: The reintroduction of exercise pulmonary hypertension (EPH) to the pulmonary hypertension (PH) definition by the European guidelines underlines the importance of examining the hemodynamic response to exercise during right heart catheterization. Because the standard exercise modality of cycle ergometry (CE) is not universally accessible, we compared its hemodynamic effects with those of dynamic single-arm exercise (AE) in patients undergoing right heart catheterization (RHC). METHODS: 50 consecutive patients with indication for RHC were enrolled. Hemodynamic parameters were assessed at rest, followed by randomized exercise periods with an intervening rest phase. Thermodilution was used to determine cardiac output. The intensity of the AE was patient-determined, whereas CE was conducted at a fixed work rate ranging from 10 to 50 watts, based on the patient's physical status. Oxygen uptake (VO₂) was estimated using the reverse Fick principle to compare relative exercise intensity between modalities. EPH was defined by an mPAP/cardiac output slope > 3 mmHg·L⁻¹·min⁻¹, and exercise-induced left heart disease by a rise in PAWP from ≤ 15 mmHg at rest to > 25 mmHg during exercise. RESULTS: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure increased by 12 mmHg with CE compared to 3 mmHg with AE (p<0.001), pulmonary artery wedge pressure increased by 5 mmHg versus 2 mmHg (p<0.001), cardiac output increased by 2.2 L/min versus 0.6 L/min (p<0.001) and mean pulmonary vascular resistance decreased by 0.05 WU with CE (p=0.761) and by 0.32 with AE (p=0.03). Estimated VO₂ during AE reached only 24% of the increase observed during CE, corresponding to an external workload equivalent of approximately 6 W. No patient showed an increase in pulmonary artery wedge pressure during exercise above 25mmHg to unmask left heart disease. In patients without PH at rest, CE led to the diagnosis of EPH in 5 patients while the used AE protocol was not suitable to detect EPH. CONCLUSION: AE proved to be a safe exercise modality in our study but, with the protocol applied here, produced significantly smaller hemodynamic changes during RHC than CE and is thus not an adequate substitute in this form, leaving open whether an intensity-matched protocol could achieve comparable hemodynamic effects.

title: Predictors of mortality in patients treated with ECMELLA after cardiac surgery – a single- center experience
authors: Nizar Salah; Matthias F. Bechtel; Justus Thomas Strauch; Vadim Moustafine; Peter Lukas Haldenwang; Dirk Buchwald; Sebastian Loesaus; Simon Becker; Peter Konrad Zahn; Dinah Maria Berres
abstract: Abstract Background Postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock (PCS) remains a serious complication after cardiac surgery associated with high perioperative mortality. Over the last years, the use of veno-arterial extracorporeal life support (VA-ECLS) combined with left ventricular unloading by a microaxial flow pump (ECMELLA) has increased. Data on mortality predictors in patients treated with ECMELLA for PCS remain limited. We aimed to identify factors associated with 30-day all-cause mortality after ECMELLA implantation. Methods We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients who received concomitant VA-ECLS and a microaxial pump after cardiac surgery at our university center between 2019 and 2024. Clinically relevant surrogate parameters were assessed along with 30-day mortality. Discriminative ability was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Survival was analyzed using Kaplan–Meier estimates with log-rank testing, and predictors of 30-day mortality were identified using univariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. Results Of the 34 patients, 26 (76.5%) died within 30 days. The Model for End-stage Liver Disease (MELD) score was significantly higher in non-survivors than in survivors (18.5 [IQR 10.7] vs. 14.9 [IQR 2.8], p = 0.010). The MELD excluding INR (MELD-XI) score was likewise higher in non-survivors (17.6 [IQR 9.7] vs. 10.2 [IQR 2.6], p = 0.001). Lactate levels were significantly lower in survivors at 12 hours (p = 0.03), 18 hours (p = 0.004) and 24 hours (p = 0.02) after ECMELLA initiation. Discrimination was best at 18 hours (AUC 0.824, p < 0.001). Aortic cross-clamp time was not associated with 30-day mortality when analyzed as a continuous variable; however, an exploratory cutoff of ≥ 63 minutes was associated with increased mortality (HR 3.20, 95% CI 1.34–7.65, p = 0.009). In univariable Cox regression, MELD-XI ≥ 12.5 (HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.13–7.32) and lactate ≥ 2 mmol/L at 18 hours (HR 4.47, 95% CI 1.48–13.52) were associated with 30-day mortality, but neither remained independently associated in multivariable analysis. Conclusions Biological markers, including MELD-XI and lactate, could provide complementary prognostic information before and after ECMELLA implantation, whereas the prognostic value of a prolonged aortic cross-clamp time, observed only in an exploratory threshold analysis, remains uncertain.

title: Association of Site Volume and MitraClip Outcomes in Secondary Mitral Regurgitation
authors: Kashish Goel; Raj R. Makkar; Hursh Naik; Satya Atmakuri; Paul Mahoney; M. Andrew Morse; Janani Aiyer; Rong Huang; Vinod H. Thourani; JoAnn Lindenfeld; Brian R. Lindman; Colin Barker
abstract: BACKGROUND: The number of sites performing transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) for secondary mitral regurgitation (SMR) has increased. Despite concerns that low-volume sites may have worse outcomes, data are limited on the association between site volume and TEER outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the association between site volume and mitral TEER outcomes in SMR. METHODS: The COAPT PAS (COAPT Post-Approval Study) included patients with SMR who underwent TEER with the MitraClip device from March 2019 to September 2020 following Food and Drug Administration approval. Sites were categorized by number of patients treated: low (≤25), medium (25-50), and high (>50). RESULTS: Of 5,000 patients, 2,632 were from low-, 1,527 from medium-, and 841 from high-volume sites. High-volume sites treated sicker patients with higher Society of Thoracic Surgeons scores and prior heart failure hospitalization rates. Procedures at low-volume sites had similar device implant rates (low: 97%, medium: 99%, high: 98%), used fewer number of clips (low: 1.4 ± 0.6, medium: 1.5 ± 0.6, high: 1.6 ± 0.7 clips, P < 0.001), and had longer device (low: 68 ± 55, medium: 56 ± 53, high: 57 ± 42 min, P < 0.001) and procedure times (low: 153 ± 67, medium: 131 ± 59, high: 128 ± 56 min, P < 0.001). Technical success was comparable (low: 93%, medium: 94%, high: 95%, P = 0.92). MR reduction to ≤2+ and ≤1+ was also similar. There was no difference in heart failure hospitalization (low: 19%, medium: 18%, high: 20%, P = 0.50) or all-cause mortality (low: 23%, medium: 21%, high: 20%, P = 0.27). CONCLUSIONS: Technical success, MR reduction, and 1-year clinical outcomes were comparable across volume strata during the early adoption phase, without significant differences between low- and high-volume centers.

title: Evaluating the reliability and quality of preeclampsia educational content on short-video platforms: a cross-sectional content analysis
authors: Shengjun You; Huangjun Ye; Zhenzhu Dong; 饶竞红; Hongling Zhang
abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a serious pregnancy-specific complication with a global incidence of 2%–8%, and is a major contributor to adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Short video platforms have emerged as important channels for the public to access health information. However, studies evaluating the quality of PE-related content on these platforms remain scarce. This study aims to assess the perceived general information quality and reliability of short videos pertaining to PE on Douyin and Bilibili, and to analyze the impacts of platform characteristics and uploader background on content quality. Employing a cross-sectional design, we searched both platforms using the keyword “preeclampsia”. Following screening, a total of 164 videos (89 from Douyin, 75 from Bilibili) were included. Video quality was evaluated using the Global Quality Scale (GQS), the modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) instrument, and the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria. The findings revealed that the unadjusted distribution of scores for GQS, mDISCERN, and JAMA varied by platform. Following adjustment for uploader category and video length, with correction for multiple comparisons, only the GQS instrument retained a significant association (Douyin vs. Bilibili: aOR = 3.917, 95% CI 1.753–8.752; adjust P -value = 0.003), while mDISCERN (adjust P -value = 0.479) and JAMA (adjust P -value = 0.053) showed no significant differences. Videos uploaded by healthcare professionals with the relevant specialty constituted 64.02% of the total sample, and these videos scored significantly higher on the mDISCERN and GQS instruments than did videos from other uploader categories; however, no significant difference was observed for the JAMA scores compared with healthcare professionals outside the relevant specialty (adjust P -value = 0.149). The video content predominantly focuses on clinical manifestations (31.10%), treatment (21.95%), and prevention (20.12%), while topics such as etiology and epidemiology accounted for less than 10% of the content. Correlation analyses stratified by platform did not reveal any consistent and statistically robust associations between engagement metrics and quality scores. The overall quality of PE-related educational content on short video platforms is below average. It is recommended that platforms strengthen the verification of credentials for science-popularization video uploaders and establish evidence-based content standards, while actively encouraging professionals to participate in health science communication. Enhancing public understanding of PE may, to some extent, improve the level of public health literacy.

title: Gonococcal Endocarditis: An Unusual Complication of Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
authors: Kevin Yum; Daniel Blankinship; Robert Gauer; David Kassop; Janelle Robertson
abstract: Gonococcal endocarditis is a rare, potentially life-threatening manifestation of disseminated Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection.Diagnosis may be delayed because patients frequently lack concurrent genitourinary symptoms.This case involves a 30-year-old active-duty U.S. Army servicemember who presented with a four-month history of intermittent fever, rigors, diaphoresis, fatigue, nonproductive cough, and mild dyspnea.He reported unprotected sexual intercourse with three female partners during the preceding six months but denied genitourinary symptoms, injection drug use, or chronic alcohol use.During hospitalization, blood cultures obtained during a febrile episode grew Neisseria gonorrhoeae.Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a mobile vegetation measuring less than 1 cm on the anterior mitral leaflet, accompanied by mild-to-moderate mitral regurgitation.The patient responded favorably to targeted antimicrobial therapy and achieved sustained clinical remission, with no evidence of recurrence at the 12month follow-up.

title: 3D bioprinting of tissues and organs for systemic diseases and localized injuries
authors: W. Kee Ng; Paulo Bártolo
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting integrates engineering, materials science, and biology to fabricate living tissues with precise spatial control. By enabling the layer-by-layer deposition of cells and biomaterials, it overcomes many limitations of traditional scaffold-based tissue engineering and offers new opportunities for regenerative and personalized medicine. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in 3D bioprinting. It introduces a systematic, ASTM-aligned classification of key bioprinting modalities, extrusion, jetting, and vat photopolymerization, along with their respective material and biological design requirements. It also summarizes recent progress in bio-ink development and crosslinking strategies that improve print fidelity and functional tissue maturation. In addition, the review highlights applications in both systemic disease modelling and treatment (such as cardiovascular, endocrine/metabolic, and neurodegenerative disorders) and localized tissue repair (including skin, musculoskeletal, cartilage, and bone), emphasizing their relevance to civilian healthcare and military medicine. By combining technological innovation, biological insights, and regulatory considerations, this review outlines how advances in multi-modal bioprinting and intelligent process control can accelerate the translation of laboratory research into clinically viable, patient-specific therapies, driving the next generation of regenerative medicine.

title: Cardiovascular complications and cardiovascular death are rare in severe COVID-19 presenting with myocardial injury or failure
authors: Connor O’Brien; Fatma Güntürkün; Yaowei Deng; Ryan Ruaysungnoen; Donald D. Chang; Sameer Khanijo; Christopher F. Barnett; Shikha Kapil; Andrea Daly; Alberto Goffi; Dekel Stavi; Francois Carrier; Yasmine Ennehas; Babar Fiza; Andrew Patterson; Thomas C. Daubert; Vanessa Moll; Clara Castellucci; Mitchell Zekhtser; Nibras Burghrara; Michaël Mayette; Karl Courchesne; Shaun Thompson; Rushi V. Parikh; Juka Kim; Melanie D. Ashland; Paul K. Mohabir
abstract: Abstract SARS-COV2 infection has been linked to cardiovascular complications. Published data suggest that cardiac injury may be a common disease feature and contribute to morbidity and mortality in severe COVID-19. Since early in the pandemic, little data has emerged describing what cardiovascular complications arise from myocardial injury in severe COVID-19 and whether these complications contribute to mortality. We set out to describe the incidence and nature of cardiovascular complications in patients with severe COVID-19 infection and biochemical or imaging evidence of myocardial injury. We analyzed consecutive patients admitted for severe COVID-19 and presenting with biochemical or echocardiographic evidence of myocardial injury across 16 centers within the CARDIO-COVID investigator-initiated consortium. A light-GBM machine learning model was used to identify variables associated with mortality. Our study included 1,328 patients. ICU mortality was 29.4%. Factors most associated with mortality were age, SOFA Cardiovascular score, elevated troponin, intubation, high vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), high PEEP, and high FiO2. Individual cardiovascular (myocardial infarction, stroke, pulmonary embolism, myocarditis, VT/VF, new onset heart failure) complications were rare (all < 5%) but common in sum (17.6%), and did not present significant association with mortality. Patients with high VIS and SOFA Cardiovascular scores had a significantly higher incidence of secondary bacterial pneumonias suggesting septic shock played a role in their physiology. Investigator-adjudicated cause of death data identified respiratory failure and septic shock as primary causes of mortality. Though cardiovascular complications of severe COVID-19 are common, they do not seem to contribute significantly to mortality. Elevated cardiac enzymes and myocardial dysfunction carry prognostic value likely reflecting myocardial strain in the setting of multisystem organ dysfunction rather than direct myocardial injury by SARS-CoV2.

title: Surgical treatment of a hypercalcemic crisis caused by a parathyroid tumor complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency: a case report
authors: Qianqian Chen; Huiling Wang
abstract: The most common cause of hypercalcemia is a parathyroid tumor (PT). These rare tumors disrupt calcium and phosphorus metabolism and cause multiorgan dysfunction; surgical resection remains the standard treatment for parathyroid tumors. This case highlights the challenges faced in the diagnosis and management of patients with complex underlying conditions: for patients experiencing a hypercalcemic crisis complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency, perioperative management presents a clinical dilemma between fluid resuscitation and cardiac tolerance, posing significant clinical challenges. A 61-year-old male patient presented with a hypercalcemic crisis caused by a parathyroid tumor, complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency. He complained of excruciating pain in the lower back and extremities, polydipsia, polyuria, and constipation. Laboratory findings showed a serum calcium level of 4.27 mmol/L, an eGFR of 15.97 mL/min/1.73 m \(^{2}\) , and an NT-proBNP level of 1771 pg/mL. Based on these laboratory findings and clinical symptoms, a hypercalcemic crisis complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency was diagnosed; imaging studies revealed a parathyroid adenoma in the right lower pole. Three months after parathyroid tumor resection, serum creatinine decreased from 340 \(\mu\) mol/L to 112 \(\mu\) mol/L. This case demonstrates that parathyroidectomy can be safely performed through the development of an individualized perioperative management plan based on multidisciplinary collaboration. The key lies in carefully balancing fluid resuscitation with cardiac tolerance, the appropriate use of diuretics, and the cautious interpretation of cardiac biomarkers such as NT-proBNP in the context of renal failure.

title: Study of Left Ventricular Remodelling in Patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
authors: Mrutyunjay B. Hiregoudar; Dhananjaya M; Raghavendra Gangaraddy; Srinivas R
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: This study aims to quantify left ventricular remodelling and the prevalence of left ventricular hypertrophy in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease devoid of cardiovascular disease. It was a hospital based cross sectional includes adult patients diagnosed with COPD belonging to all classes of GOLD criteria which includes both OPD and IPD cases at SDMCMS&H. Patients with CAD, cardiomyopathy, LBBB , heart failure, significant valvular dysfunction , chronic AF, pacemaker , hypertension higher than stage1 and IDDM were excluded. Sample size is 150 . Thorough history , clinical examination , ECG , chest xray , echocardiography done. In the echocardiography interventricular septal wall thickness(SWT), posterior wall thickness (PWT) , left ventricular end diastolic diameter (EDD) , LVH noted. LVM and RWT calculated using appropriate formula . Results: In the present study , we noted that the mean age in the study was 70.24 years. In that 62% were males and 28% were females with male to female ratio of 1.63:1 . The mean SWT was 11.36mm , mean PWT- 11.15mm , mean LVEDD- 39.15mm. The RWT was below 0.42 in 4.67% of patients and above 0.42 in 95.33% subjects. Of the remodelling types observed 2% exhibited eccentric LVH and 98% concentric LVH. The average LVM – 202.87. CONCLUSION: By evaluating LVM and RWT, we aimed to quantify LV remodeling and the prevalence of LVH in COPD. The majority (95.33%) had a relative wall thickness greater than 0.42, with a high sensitivity (94.3%) and specificity (95.2%). Most subjects (98%) exhibited concentric LVH, and the left ventricular mass averaged 202.87, ranging from 62.10 to 529.63. These findings highlight significant demographic, clinical, and cardiac characteristics of the study population.

title: Pediatric Cardiac Surgery in the Pre-Conflict Era: A Retrospective Analysis of the Surgical patterns and outcomes Medani Heart Center, Sudan (2019–2022)
authors: Salah Hassan; Awab Mohieldeen; Mohamed Fargalla; Babekir Elmostafa; Yousry Mohammed
abstract: Abstract Background Pediatric cardiac care in sub-Saharan Africa is characterized by a significant surgical-medical gap, where late referrals and infrastructural limitations complicate outcomes for congenital and acquired heart disease. While Medani Heart Center (MHC) emerged as a critical tertiary referral hub in Sudan to address these geographic and systemic barriers, the 2023 conflict has fundamentally disrupted these specialized services. Documenting the clinical and procedural patterns established prior to this crisis is essential to providing a baseline for assessing current survival gaps and guiding future service restoration. This study evaluates the surgical patterns, patient demographics, and perioperative outcomes of pediatric cardiac patients managed at the MHC between 2019 and 2022. Methods We conducted a retrospective, observational cohort study of pediatric patients aged under 18 years who underwent cardiac surgical intervention at the Medani Heart Center (MHC), Sudan, between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2022. Data were retrieved from the center’s official registry for 250 patients who met the inclusion criteria. Although the study was intended to extend into 2023, data from January 2023 onward were lost due to the destruction of the center's infrastructure during the national conflict. This analysis represents the final, verified clinical record of the MHC’s pediatric cardiac services prior to the suspension of operations. Results Among the 250 pediatric cardiac surgical patients analyzed, the majority were males (54.8%) and predominantly school-age children (54.0%). Procedures comprised structural congenital repairs (ventricular septal defect [VSD] 24.4%, atrial septal defect [ASD] 10.0%, patent ductus arteriosus [PDA] 9.2%), complex cyanotic anomaly corrections (Tetralogy of Fallot 18.8%), and valvular interventions (23.6%). Surgical volume peaked in 2021 (38.4%) before stabilizing in 2022. Post-operative outcomes were largely favorable, with 83.6% of patients experiencing an uneventful recovery and 87.2% requiring an intensive care unit (ICU) stay of 5 days or fewer. The overall mortality rate was 4.0%. Conclusion This study confirms that a high-volume regional pediatric cardiac surgical program can deliver efficient, high-quality care, evidenced by an 83.6% complication-free recovery rate and streamlined ICU management. The surge and subsequent stabilization of procedural volumes indicate a maturing clinical workflow capable of managing complex congenital and valvular cases. These findings validate the effectiveness of past clinical protocols while highlighting an essential baseline for future cardiovascular care reconstruction in the region. Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

title: Peripheral Artery Disease in Acute Care Settings: Diagnosis and Management of Common Presentations and Emergencies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
authors: Jennifer A. Rymer; Subhash Banerjee; Joshua Beckman; Abdulla A. Damluji; Katharine L. McGinigle; Lee Kirksey; Sahil Parikh; Alexander E. Sullivan; Debra Kohlman-Trigoboff; L. Wilkins; Eric Secemsky
abstract: People with peripheral artery disease (PAD) are often misdiagnosed or diagnosed late and, even after diagnosis, are undertreated with both pharmacologic and invasive therapies. The disease is associated with an increased risk of mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, other vascular disease, limb loss, and reduced quality of life. Although the risks and long-term management of PAD are well documented, these risks are acutely magnified when PAD exists as a comorbidity in patients hospitalized for other cardiovascular or medical conditions. Procedures requiring vascular access for the treatment of acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, or valvular heart disease, as well as procedures for the treatment of the patient's underlying PAD, require special consideration in patients with PAD. Familiarity with the use and placement of mechanical circulatory support in patients with PAD, as well as the management of recent endovascular or surgical vascular interventions, is essential for providing appropriate care in the acute care setting.

title: Incidence and predictors of heart failure among anthracycline-treated older adults with lymphoma
authors: Jenica N. Upshaw; Angie Mae Rodday; Cara Guardino; Benjamin Sweigart; Jason Nelson; Anita J. Kumar; Marvin A Konstam; Bonnie Ky; Jonathan W. Friedberg; Andrew M. Evens; David M. Kent; Susan Kenyon Parsons
abstract: Anthracycline-based chemotherapy is recommended in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) but can cause heart failure (HF), especially in older patients who have increased risk due to age and comorbidities. To estimate the risk of incident HF in older DLBCL or cHL patients. Using SEER-Medicare, we identified individuals 65 years of age and older diagnosed with DLBCL or cHL between 2000–2015 who received anthracycline-containing therapy and were free of preexisting HF. Incident HF and HF hospitalization were ascertained from billing codes using validated algorithms. Separate multivariate risk prediction models were developed for the outcomes of 1) incident HF and 2) HF hospitalization using Fine and Gray models that account for the competing risk of death. Among 13,401 individuals with newly diagnosed DLBCL or cHL (mean age 75.1 ± 6.1 years, 49.1% female), we observed 3,343 incident HF diagnoses over a median (IQR) follow-up of 2.7 (0.8, 6.1) years. Two and 5-year estimates of incident HF diagnoses after anthracycline were 14.2% (95% CI 13.6–14.8%) and 21.6% (95% CI 20.9–22.3%), respectively, and 2-year cumulative incidence of HF hospitalization was 9.6% (95% CI 9.1–10.1%) in models accounting for the competing risk of death. Older age, cHL diagnosis, hypertension, diabetes, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and peripheral vascular disease were associated with higher incident HF. The optimism-corrected c-statistic was 0.60 (95% CI 0.59, 0.61). Incident HF occurred in more than 14% of older patients with DLBCL or cHL within two years after diagnosis and common cardiac comorbidities predict increased HF risk. Future studies incorporating baseline echocardiographic measures may improve model performance.

title: The Impact of Cardiac Surgery on Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms
authors: Mikołaj Czerwonka; Mateusz Sobierajski; Wiktoria Sochal; Julia Kot
abstract: Background: Cardiac surgery is associated with physical recovery demands and psychological distress. Anxiety and depressive symptoms may be present before surgery, change during rehabilitation or persist after discharge. Aim: To review the frequency of anxiety and depressive symptoms after cardiac surgery, factors associated with their occurrence and the effects of supportive interventions. Methods: To identify articles on anxiety and depressive symptoms following cardiac surgery, the PubMed, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar databases were searched. Only English-language publications were included. Results: In a retrospective study of 132,390 cardiac surgery patients, 12.6% had newly documented depression or an antidepressant prescription within one year. In a prospective CABG subgroup, 13 of 89 patients (14.6%) developed depression during follow-up. Early esketamine and dexmedetomidine trials showed lower proportions of positive depression and anxiety screens shortly after surgery, but some effects did not persist. Rehabilitation, education and psychological support were associated with symptom improvement. Conclusions: Psychological assessment before and after cardiac surgery should distinguish new diagnoses from questionnaire scores. Available findings support individualized follow-up but do not establish the operation itself as the sole cause of subsequent depression or anxiety.

title: Artificial intelligence driven software systems for cardiovascular disease detection using physiological signals: a systematic review
authors: MD Tasnim Alam; Abdullah Al-Mamun Bulbul; Md Ismail Hossen; A. K. M. Azad; Asaduzzaman Khan; Mohammad Ali Moni
abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular disease exacts an extraordinary global toll, with annual mortality exceeding 17.9 million lives and representing nearly one-third of all deaths worldwide. Reducing diagnostic delays, particularly in resource-limited settings, requires innovative, scalable, and cost-effective solutions. Artificial intelligence integrated with physiological signals, such as electrocardiogram (ECG), photoplethysmogram (PPG) and phonocardiogram (PCG), offers promising pathways for scalable, real-time cardiovascular assessment. Despite rapid advances, the evidence base remains fragmented, impeding identification of validated approaches and clinical translation pathways. A PRISMA-guided search across five databases (Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, IEEE Xplore) identified 35 eligible peer-reviewed studies. Quality and risk of bias were appraised using a QUADAS-2 adapted framework. Most systems utilised ECG (71.4%) with deep learning architectures, including convolutional and recurrent neural networks. Critical gaps were quantified: only 23% of studies conducted external validation, only 14% achieved clinical-scale deployment, no study integrated principled multi-signal fusion (ECG + PPG + PCG), and only one system (1/35, 2.9%) implemented a patient-facing conversational interface. Reported accuracies ranged from 70.5 to 99.9% (n = 21 reporting; unweighted mean 93.7%), but inconsistent metric reporting and limited external validation tempered translational confidence. A three-directional framework is proposed, addressing generalisability through multi-signal (ECG + PPG + PCG) models, interpretability through LLM-driven clinical narratives, and accessibility through edge-cloud deployment, to guide future research toward clinically deployable systems.
